youtube_title: The Contract Only One Side Can Undo — If They're Under 18 🦝⚖️
caption: California Family Code 6710 lets a minor disaffirm most contracts before 18 or within a reasonable time after — with exceptions for necessities and court-approved entertainment contracts.
script: There's a contract you can walk away from whenever you want, if you're under eighteen. [disclaimer] This is California law. Under the state's Family Code, unless another statute says otherwise, a contract made by a minor can be canceled by the minor before turning eighteen, or within a reasonable time afterward. Lawyers call that disaffirming the contract. So imagine a sixteen-year-old signs a deal with an adult business. The adult is generally held to it. The minor may be able to walk away. That's not a glitch. It's a deliberate protection for minors. But there are big exceptions. A minor generally can't cancel a contract to pay the reasonable value of necessities, things needed for their support or their family's, if those things were actually provided, and the minor wasn't under the care of a parent or guardian who could provide them. And certain entertainment contracts can be approved by a court. Once a court approves one, it can't be canceled just because the person was a minor. Other statutes create more exceptions. And the escape hatch isn't a license for fraud, or a way to keep everything with no consequences. Other laws can still apply. So the hatch is real, but it's narrower than the internet makes it sound. [loop] So before you sign a deal with a sixteen-year-old, remember
